**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes the origin back only if it is one of these:

- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

Everything else gets `null`, so the browser blocks it. A request with no `Origin` header also gets `null`. Non-browser clients aren't affected, because CORS is only enforced by browsers.

Other CORS settings in the same block:
- Methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`.
- Headers: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`.
- `maxAge`: 86400.

**To add a custom domain**, edit the condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add one of these inside the `if (...)`:

- For an exact origin, add `|| origin === 'https://app.example.com'`. Include the scheme and no trailing slash.
- For all subdomains, add `|| origin.endsWith('.example.com')`.

The `endsWith` form is looser than it looks. `.example.com` matches any subdomain, and the existing `.pages.dev` and `.workers.dev` checks are broad in the same way. Prefer the exact match for a single custom domain.

I only searched `worker/` for origin and CORS handling, so I haven't checked whether the frontend has its own API base URL that also needs updating. Redeploy the worker after the change.
